transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling like… the best part of my life is probably behind me. Not in a dramatic way, just this steady feeling that no matter how much I plan or try to be disciplined, I’m not going to get back to feeling like myself.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure I’d say that exactly. I still can enjoy things at times. It’s more that I don’t feel as upbeat about them as I used to, but I haven’t really noticed a clear loss of interest.
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the time, even when things are going okay?

Yes. Most days I wouldn’t say I’m crying or anything like that, but there’s this low, gray feeling underneath things. Even when things are fine—like if I’m in the studio or having dinner with my wife—it’s still sort of there.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you’re not doing much?

Yes, I have. I still get up and do what I need to do—shopping, little projects around the house, that sort of thing—but I get worn out more easily than I think I should. Even setting up for a mentoring session or walking around a community event can leave me drained, and a nap doesn’t really seem to reset it.
Have you been feeling more critical of yourself lately, or like you’re not measuring up in areas that are important to you?
I don’t think so, not especially. I mean, I can get frustrated with myself like anyone, but I haven’t noticed a real pattern of beating myself up or feeling like I’m failing at things that matter.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Not really, no. I mean, I have the usual moments where I walk into a room and forget why, or take a little longer to choose something, but I haven’t noticed a clear change in my focus or thinking. Nothing that stands out to me.

Have you noticed that you’re not looking forward to things as much as you used to, or that you’re not getting the same satisfaction out of your usual activities, even if you still enjoy them a little?

I’m not sure I’d say that. I still get some enjoyment out of the things I usually do. Maybe I don’t get excited about them the way some people do, but I haven’t really noticed a clear change where I’m not looking forward to things or they don’t feel satisfying anymore.
Can you describe how long this low, gray feeling tends to last on most days? Is it something that stays with you throughout the day, or does it come and go?

Most days it’s kind of there in the background. I’m not crying or anything dramatic like that, but there’s this low, gray feeling underneath things. Even if I’m in the studio or sitting at dinner with my wife, it can still be there. It may not be strong every minute, but it tends to hang around.
How long has this low, gray feeling been going on? Have you felt this way for most of the day, more days than not, for at least the past two years?
Yes. It started after my hiking injury, a little over three years ago. So… about three years and three months now. It’s been there most days since then.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, or feelings of hopelessness during this time?

The main thing is the hopelessness. I wouldn’t say it’s dramatic, but it’s been getting harder to shake this feeling that the best part of my life is behind me. Like no matter how much I plan or try to stay disciplined, I’m not going to get back to feeling like myself again.

inference_history.note: The patient describes a persistent feeling that the best part of their life is behind them and a lack of hope in returning to feeling like themselves, which suggests possible depressive symptoms. This supports consideration of Major Depressive Disorder (F32.9, F33.9) and Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood (F43.22). No sufficient information yet to rule out or confirm specific diagnoses.
